title: Turf War
one_paragraph_synopsis: In "Turf War," tensions rise as the Binghamton branch closes, sparking a dispute over client territories between the Scranton and Syracuse branches. Jim, Dwight, and others engage in humorous and competitive antics, including a flat curl contest and the creation of a fictional salesman to circumvent commission caps. Robert, the CEO, delays decisions on dividing clients and forbids contact with key accounts, while Andy attempts to secure a major client and pitch an investment. Meanwhile, Pam uncovers Nellie's personal struggles, adding emotional depth to the office dynamics. The episode ends with several unresolved conflicts and decisions pending.

main_threads.thread: The closure of the Binghamton branch leads to a turf war between the Scranton and Syracuse branches over client territories, with Robert delaying decisions and forbidding contact with key clients.

evidence.snippet: Jim: Binghamton branch closed last night and their clients are up for grabs.
Robert: Closing the Binghamton branch never occurred to me before today.
I have decided. Neither of you are to have any contact with either Prestige or any other Binghamton client until I have figured out how to divide things up.
Dwight: Prestige is ours. Okay, they're responsible for half of the junk mail on the eastern seaboard. We get them.
Jim: How about this? How about we just ask Robert? Can we all agree that maybe the C.E.O should decide this?
Harry: Robert's here. Look at us. BickEring like schoolgirls, looking around the room for things to hit each other with.

main_threads.thread: Jim, Dwight, and Gabe engage in humorous competition and schemes, including a flat curl contest to determine strength and inventing a fictional salesman, Lloyd Gross, to manipulate commissions.

evidence.snippet: Gabe: Ugh, man. My delts are blasted. I wish they had a chart for how much protein powder to scoop for a 180 pound man with no fat.
Dwight: Protein powder, huh? You cut it with water? Why don't you just take estrogen?
Jim: Listen, guys, I think we all want to know the same thing, right? Who's the strongest? Well, there's only one way to solve that – flat curl contest.
Jim: All right, here we go everybody. May the manliest man win. Go.
Dwight: Lloyd Gross is a fictional salesman we invented to – how do I put this – steal from the company. Embezzle. To commit fraud.
Jim: Pam made a drawing of Lloyd. He is a blend of all the salesman.

main_threads.thread: Andy attempts to secure the Prestige client and later pitches Dunder Mifflin as an investment to David, facing rejection and insults from Robert but gaining a potential opportunity with David.

evidence.snippet: Andy: That was a fine branch. Things are really bad under Robert California, I guess. It's like a festival of poo.
Andy: I'm a former paper executive. I know the product. I know the margins. I can save you 25% on your costs.
Andy: Of course they have. Which is why I'm giving you a key to my house. Whatever you need – anytime, night or day – you just stop on by.
Robert: Ah, well, I will not be blackmailed by some ineffectual, privileged, effete, soft-penised debutante.
Andy: I wanted to see if I could interest you in an investment. Dunder Mifflin.
David: Why don't you come in?

main_threads.thread: Pam discovers Nellie's financial and emotional struggles by stealing her phone and deleting troubling messages, leading to a candid conversation about Nellie's issues and her negative view of Robert.

evidence.snippet: Pam: I stole Nellie's phone.
Phone: This is MasterCard. You are over the limit. Send the minimum payment of $448 by Monday, or we will be forced to send it to collections.
Pam: No. My goodness. You have a lot going on. With Robert and everything.

main_threads.thread: Dwight's attempts to secure new clients fail when Mr. Ramish chooses a new supplier, and Dwight and Harry engage in banter about their partnership and dating status.

evidence.snippet: Dwight K. Schrute. Dunder Mifflin, Scranton. Forgive my pants, they fell down. An appointment with Mr. Ramish, please.
Let me stop you all right here. I've already picked a new paper supplier.
Harry: You know, your partner's got a lotta attitude. But I like that. How long you guys been dating?
Dwight: Jim couldn't land me in a thousand years.
